title: SedDNA results along the sediment core of the Dzoumogné reservoir
author: Foucher, Anthony
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0
materials: This repository is made up of two main folders containing information about the metadata and the database variables: Metadata_SedDNA_dzoumogne_reservoir_afoucher.xlsx (description of the metadata associated with the sediment samples) Variable_description_dzoumogne_reservoir_afoucher.xlsx (description of the database variables) as well as 6 folders containing the data sets for each genetic marker: Balitzki_12S-afoucher.xlsx Hardy_18S-afoucher.xlsx Kelly_16S-afoucher.xlsx Pornon_ITS-afoucher.xlsx Prosser_rtbl-afoucher.xlsx White_ITS-afoucher.xlsx Related publication: Foucher et al. submitted --------------------------------------------------------- Context: Sediment DNA was extracted from 12 layers along a sediment core ( IGSN number: 10.58052/IEFOU0003 ) collected in 2021 in the Dzoumogné reservoir (Mayotte Island, Comoros Archipelago, France), covering the 2012-2021 period. The aim of these analyses was to evaluate the consequences of landscape defragmentation, induced by deforestation and intensification of agricultural practices, on changes in biological communities. Sample collection, storage and subsampling: Sediment core was collected using an Uwitec gravity corer equipped with a 63mm PVC liner. The core was stored at 4°C in a cold and dark room for 3 weeks prior to subsampling. The sediment core was opened and subsampled in a previously sterilized hoot (DNA cleaner and UV) in a dedicated biological room at the University of Paris-Saclay. Each sample was extracted from the sediment core using sterilized metal plates inserted on either side of the layer to be sampled (the central part of this sample was then sub-sampled to remove the part of the sediment in contact with the PVC tube of the core and the cutting tools). During this process the operators were equipped with gloves, masks and headgear to avoid any risk of contamination. A blank was placed in the fume cupboard to control contamination during core opening and sampling. Extraction and assignation: Sed DNA was retrieved using a standardized protocol that combines the use of commercial kits (Nucleospin soil – Macherey-Nagel) and the extracellular DNA pre-treatment described in Taberlet et al. (1). In order to limit amplification biases and to improve the metabarcoding sensitivity, a combination of 7 genetic markers was used to PCR-amplify each targeted taxonomic group (plants - 50-70 bp – trnL (2), plants - 150 bp – rbcL (3), plants/fungi – 320 bp –ITS (4), plants – 380 bp – ITS , metazoa – 200 bp – 16S (5), Eukaryotes – 200 bp – 18S (6), vertebrates – 200 bp – 12S (7)). PCRs were realized in octuplicates with positive and negative controls. Extraction controls were also amplified with the dedicated primers. PCR products were cleaned using the MinElute purification kit (QIAGEN) and all purified amplicons were pooled in equimolar concentrations at the exception of the extraction and the PCR negative controls as they were not concentrated enough. Then, each sample pool was run on an Agilent Bioanalyzer using the DNA High Sensitivity LabChip kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA) to verify amplicon length and each sample was finally quantified with a Qubit fluorometer (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA). Libraries were generated with a PCR-free protocol in order to tremendously reduce the number of chimeras induced by the metabarcoding approach. One microgram of each purified PCR products pool was submitted to molecular end-repair and then ligated to Illumina adapters prior to sequencing on Illumina platforms (Next-Generation Sequencing; Fasteris, Switzerland) using a NovaSeq instrument (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA) with a paired-end read mode covering the amplicon lengths. steps.title: Collect sediment core
steps.instruction: Use an Uwitec gravity corer equipped with a 63 mm PVC liner to retrieve a sediment core from the Dzoumogné reservoir (IGSN 10.58052/IEFOU0003) in 2021.

steps.title: Store core before subsampling
steps.instruction: Place the intact core in a cold, dark room at 4 °C and keep it for 3 weeks prior to any subsampling.

steps.title: Open core and subsample under sterile conditions
steps.instruction: In a dedicated biological room, open the core inside a DNA‑cleaner UV‑sterilized hood. Wear gloves, masks and headgear. Insert sterilized metal plates on either side of each layer to be sampled, then remove the central portion of sediment, discarding the part that contacted the PVC tube and cutting tools. Place a blank sample in the fume cupboard to monitor contamination.

steps.title: Extract extracellular sediment DNA
steps.instruction: Apply the standardized extraction protocol that combines the Nucleospin Soil kit (Macherey‑Nagel) with the extracellular DNA pre‑treatment described by Taberlet et al. (2012). Include extraction blanks and amplify extraction controls with the dedicated primers.

steps.title: Set up multiplex PCR for seven markers
steps.instruction: Prepare PCR mixes for the following seven genetic markers: trnL (plants, 50‑70 bp), rbcL (plants, 150 bp), ITS (plants/fungi, 320 bp), ITS (plants, 380 bp), 16S (metazoa, 200 bp), 18S (eukaryotes, 200 bp), 12S (vertebrates, 200 bp).

steps.title: Perform PCR in octuplicate with controls
steps.instruction: Run each PCR in eight replicates (octuplicates) together with positive and negative controls. Also amplify the extraction blanks using the same primer sets.

steps.title: Clean PCR products and pool amplicons
steps.instruction: Purify all PCR products with the MinElute purification kit (QIAGEN). Pool the purified amplicons from each sample in equimolar concentrations, except for extraction blanks and PCR negative controls, which are omitted because they were not concentrated enough.

steps.title: Verify amplicon size and quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Run each pooled sample on an Agilent Bioanalyzer using the DNA High Sensitivity LabChip kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA) to check amplicon length. Then quantify the DNA with a Qubit fluorometer (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA).

steps.title: Prepare PCR‑free sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Using a PCR‑free protocol, take 1 µg of each purified pooled amplicon, perform molecular end‑repair, and ligate Illumina adapters to the repaired ends.

steps.title: Sequence libraries on Illumina NovaSeq
steps.instruction: Submit the adapter‑ligated libraries to Fasteris (Switzerland) for sequencing on an Illumina NovaSeq instrument (San Diego, CA, USA) in paired‑end mode covering the full amplicon lengths, targeting approximately 1 million reads per marker per sample.

steps.title: Process reads with OBITools and QIIME2
steps.instruction: Demultiplex raw reads using OBITools, remove erroneous sequences, filter out singletons, and cluster the remaining sequences at 97 % identity with VSEARCH. Discard any sequences that appear in the extraction blanks.

steps.title: Assign taxonomy via BLAST and Bayesian classifier
steps.instruction: First, blast the clustered sequences against a custom GenBank‑derived database; retain hits with >95 % identity and compute their last common ancestor with MEGAN. Second, run a Naïve Bayesian classifier using QIIME’s rescript plugin for a complementary taxonomic assignment.
